Kaplan–Meier curves summarize time-to-event data: the step-down survival probability over
time, usually split by a group like treatment arm. In this post we build one in R with
[canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org). canvasXpress computes the survival steps for you —
you hand it a **time** column and a **censoring** column, and it does the rest — and the
result is an interactive figure that serializes to one portable, reproducible spec.

## A survival table

Swap this simulated block for your own data: you need, per subject, a follow-up **time**, a
**censoring indicator** (1 = censored, 0 = event), and the grouping variable.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

set.seed(1)
n    <- 200
arm  <- sample(c("Treatment", "Control"), n, replace = TRUE)
base <- ifelse(arm == "Treatment", 60, 40)      # treatment survives longer
time <- round(rexp(n, rate = 1 / base), 1)
cens <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.3)                        # 1 = censored, 0 = event
subj <- paste0("Subj", seq_len(n))
```

canvasXpress reads two columns for a Kaplan–Meier plot — the time and its matching censor
flag — plus a per-subject annotation carrying the group.

```{r}
y <- data.frame(
  "Time"        = time,
  "Time-Censor" = cens,
  row.names     = subj,
  check.names   = FALSE
)

varAnnot <- data.frame(Arm = arm, row.names = subj, check.names = FALSE)
```

## The plot

The key is `graphType = "KaplanMeier"` and passing **both** columns to `xAxis` (time first,
then the censor column). `colorBy` stratifies the curves.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data     = y,
  varAnnot = varAnnot,
  graphType = "KaplanMeier",
  xAxis    = list("Time", "Time-Censor"),
  colorBy  = "Arm",
  title    = "Overall survival by treatment arm",
  xAxisTitle = "Time (weeks)",
  yAxisTitle = "Probability of survival",
  invertCensored = TRUE,     # draw censoring ticks
  showKMConfidenceIntervals = FALSE,
  width  = 650,
  height = 500
)
```

Hover any step for the time and survival probability; the tick marks are censored subjects.
Because canvasXpress derives the survival curve from the raw table, you never precompute the
steps — and the same spec re-renders the identical curve from Python or JavaScript.

## A common gotcha

The survival transform only fires with `graphType = "KaplanMeier"`. If you use a bare
`"Scatter2D"` you'll get a raw scatter of the censor values instead — survival probability is
*computed* by the engine, it is not a column in your data.
